PROPOSAL: Compare token embeddings (learned or pre-trained) between U-Net-based diffusion models and DiTs to understand the representational differences between language-like and image-like tokens. TITLE: DiT-MoE with Spatial-Aware Routing
PROPOSAL: Implement a spatial-aware routing module for DiT-MoE, which dynamically aggregates spatial features from the intermediate diffusion layers to guide the token routing process. This can be achieved by using a spatial attention mechanism to learn weighted sums of tokens from expert modules in sequential neighborhoods.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original DiT-MoE, DiT-MoE with spatial attention, and DiT-MoE with spatial-aware routing. Evaluate performance on real-world text-to-image generation datasets such as DALL-E, ALICE-Train, and ALICE-Test, as well as query costs, active parameters, memory usage, etc. (metrics for efficiency).
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance in text-to-image generation tasks when using spatial-aware routing, with a potential increase in performance across various metrics. However, this may come at the cost of increased computational complexity and memory usage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: SmartToken: A New Token Representation for Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel token representation, called SmartToken, which combines the benefits of discrete and continuous token representations. SmartTokens are derived from the spatial features of the input image and are designed to be more informative and interpretable than traditional tokens. In addition, we propose a new routing mechanism that utilizes the spatial structure of SmartTokens to guide the token routing process.
CONTROLS: Evaluate SmartToken on various metrics, including generation quality, diversity, and efficiency, compared to traditional tokens and other MoE routing mechanisms. Measure improvements in terms of increased generation quality, reduced hallucinations, and better expert specialization. Test on real-world datasets, such as FFHQ, CelebA, and DALL-E.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect SmartToken to outperform traditional tokens and other routing mechanisms in terms of generation quality and diversity, with improved expert specialization and reduced hallucinations. However, the development and training of SmartToken may require significant additional computational resources.

TITLE: Expert Specialization through Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of knowledge distillation to improve expert specialization in DiT-MoE architectures. Utilize a teacher-student framework, where a pre-trained expert module serves as the teacher, and the student module learns to approximate the teacher's behavior through knowledge distillation. We will evaluate the quality of expert specialization and model performance on real-world text-to-image generation datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare to the baseline DiT-MoE architecture, as well as other expert specialization techniques (e.g., SmartToken). Measure improvements in terms of increased expert specialization, reduced hallucinations, and improved generation quality. Evaluate the effectiveness of knowledge distillation across different teacher-student architectures and hyperparameter settings.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect knowledge distillation to improve expert specialization and model performance, leading to better quality images and reduced hallucinations. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation may depend on the quality of the teacher model and hyperparameter settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Expert Routing Decisions through Visualizations and Explainability Techniques
PROPOSAL: Visualize and analyze the routing decisions made by the expert modules in DiT-MoE architectures using techniques such as t-SNE, PCA, and SHAP. This will help us understand the patterns and relationships between expert modules, tokens, and routing decisions. Additionally, we will apply explainability techniques such as feature importance and partial dependence plots to identify the features that are most influential in the expert routing decisions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the effectiveness of visualizations and explainability techniques in understanding expert routing decisions. Measure improvements in terms of increased interpretability, reduced hallucinations, and improved generation quality. Compare to baseline DiT-MoE architecture and other expert specialization techniques (e.g., SmartToken, knowledge distillation).
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect visualizations and explainability techniques to provide valuable insights into expert routing decisions, leading to better understanding of the model's behavior and potential improvements in generation quality and reduce hallucinations. However, the interpretability and accuracy of these techniques may depend on the quality of the data and the complexity of the model.

TITLE: Evaluating the Scalability of DiT-MoE Architectures with Large Numbers of Experts
PROPOSAL: Investigate the scalability of DiT-MoE architectures with large numbers of experts (e.g., 100, 200, 500) using techniques such as efficiency measurements, memory requirements, and computational resources. We will evaluate the impact of increasing the number of experts on model performance, generation quality, and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare to baseline DiT-MoE architecture with a smaller number of experts (e.g., 10, 20, 50). Measure improvements in terms of increased model size, computational resources, and generation quality.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect DiT-MoE architectures with larger numbers of experts to achieve better generation quality and model capacity at the cost of increased computational resources and memory requirements. However, the optimal number of experts may depend on the specific task, dataset, and model architecture.

TITLE: Comparing MoE Architectures for DiTs: A Comprehensive Study
PROPOSAL: Combine the results from previous experiments and compare the performance of different MoE architectures for DiTs, including vanilla DiT-MoE, DiT-MoE with spatial-aware routing, SmartToken, expert specialization through knowledge distillation, and analyzing expert routing decisions through visualizations and explainability techniques. We will also evaluate the impact of increasing the number of experts on model performance, generation quality, and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare to baseline DiT architecture. Measure improvements in terms of increased generation quality, efficiency, and model capacity.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect MoE architectures to significantly outperform the baseline DiT architecture in terms of generation quality, efficiency, and model capacity. The results from this study will provide a comprehensive understanding of the strengths and limitations of different MoE architectures for DiTs and will guide future research in this area.

TITLE: Exploring Hyperparameter Tuning for MoE Routing in DiT
PROPOSAL: We will apply a range of tuning algorithms (Grid Search, Random Search, Bayesian Optimization, and Evolution Strategies) to the existing MoE routing mechanisms (token-choice routing and expert-choice routing) in DiT-MoE and EC-DiT, using the Dataset for Improved BSS protocols Images ( DI-BSS-I) and a variety of Image FID scores and Inception Scores as objective functions to find optimal hyperparameters.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT baselines (DiT-B5, DiT-RL-UPO); unoptimized MoE implementations (EC-DiT and DiT-MoE);
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating state-of-the-art hyperparameter tuning techniques, we can improve the Image FID score of EC-DiT by up to 20% and DiT-MoE by up to 30%, narrowing the gap with their dense DiT counterparts. Failure might arise if the tuning algorithms fail to capture the complex interactions between routing and topological transformation patterns within DiT models.

TITLE: Comparing Routing Mechanisms for MoE in DiT on Challenging Image-Conditional Text-to-Image Datasets
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the token-choice routing and expert-choice routing mechanisms in DiT-MoE and EC-DiT on challenging image-conditional text-to-image datasets, specifically on the "COCO+Animals" and "Laion400M-OCD" datasets, with metrics including Inception Score, Perceptual Path Length, and relative sampling efficiency. To assess the generalizability of our findings, we will consider both standard training and few-shot transfer learning settings.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT baselines (DiT-B5, DiT-RL-UPO) on COCO+Animals and Laion400M-OCD; baseline results from prior experiments on DI-BSS-I;
COST: 1800 GPU-hours

Potential issues may arise when difficulties occur in finding a stable balance between local feature preservation and prior consistency within episodic settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert Specialization via Cluster-Based Routing for DiT-MoE
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel routing mechanism for DiT-MoE that clusters visual tokens into distinct groups based on their semantic meaning, spatial relationships, and other visual properties. Each expert is then assigned to a specific cluster, enabling them to specialize in processing tokens with similar characteristics. We evaluate our approach on the ImageNet and COCO+Animals datasets and compare its performance with state-of-the-art routing methods.
CONTROLS: 1. Baseline results from prior experiments on token-choice routing and expert-choice routing; 2. Dense DiT baseline (DiT-B6); 3. Cluster-Based Routing variants with different cluster numbers and initialization strategies.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our cluster-based routing approach significantly improves the performance of DiT-MoE, achieving a 30% boost in ImageNet FID score and a 20% improvement in COCO+Animals Inception Score, while also reducing computational overhead. Potential issues may arise when determining the optimal cluster number or initialization strategy.

TITLE: MoE Training Regimens for DiT: A Comparison of Decoupled and Joint Optimization
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of different training regimens on the performance of MoE-based DiT models. Specifically, we compare decoupled optimization, where experts are trained individually, and joint optimization, where the entire MoE network is trained together. We evaluate these approaches on the ImageNet and COCO+Animals datasets and assess their convergence rate, parameter efficiency, and final performance.
CONTROLS: 1. Baseline results from prior experiments on token-choice routing and expert-choice routing; 2. Dense DiT baseline (DiT-B6); 3. Expert Specialization via Cluster-Based Routing for DiT-MoE (turn 6).
COST: 3200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our results show that joint optimization leads to faster convergence and better final performance, but with increased computational overhead. Decoupled optimization, on the other hand, may lead to over-specialization, hindering the overall performance of the MoE model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Expert Overlap on MoE Performance in DiT
PROPOSAL: We investigate the relationship between expert overlap and MoE performance in DiT models. We propose a novel metric to quantify expert overlap and analyze its impact on MoE performance using the ImageNet and COCO+Animals datasets. We explore the effects of different expert overlap rates and strategies to mitigate its negative impact on MoE performance.
CONTROLS: 1. Baseline results from prior experiments on token-choice routing and expert-choice routing; 2. Expert Specialization via Cluster-Based Routing for DiT-MoE (turn 6); 3. MoE Training Regimens for DiT: A Comparison of Decoupled and Joint Optimization (turn 7).
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our results show that expert overlap can significantly degrade MoE performance, but we also identify strategies to mitigate its impact, such as increasing the number of experts or using a hierarchical routing mechanism.

TITLE: Evaluating MoE for Scalable and Efficient Text-to-Image Synthesis with DiT
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the performance of MoE-based DiT models on large-scale text-to-image synthesis tasks, such as generating high-resolution images from detailed text descriptions. We compare the performance of MoE-based DiT models with dense DiT models on the LAION-400M dataset and assess their computational efficiency, image quality, and diversity.
CONTROLS: 1. Baseline results from prior experiments on token-choice routing and expert-choice routing; 2. Expert Specialization via Cluster-Based Routing for DiT-MoE (turn 6); 3. MoE Training Regimens for DiT: A Comparison of Decoupled and Joint Optimization (turn 7).
COST: 4000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our results show that MoE-based DiT models can achieve superior performance on large-scale text-to-image synthesis tasks while maintaining computational efficiency, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and training regimens to achieve optimal performance.

TITLE: A Comprehensive Framework for Improving MoE Performance in Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We integrate the insights and methods developed throughout this project into a comprehensive framework for improving MoE performance in DiT models. Our framework, called MoE-DiT, includes hyperparameter tuning, expert specialization, joint optimization, and a novel expert overlap mitigation strategy. We evaluate MoE-DiT on a variety of text-to-image synthesis tasks and demonstrate improved performance compared to state-of-the-art DiT models.
CONTROLS: 1. Baseline results from prior experiments on token-choice routing and expert-choice routing; 2. Expert Specialization via Cluster-Based Routing for DiT-MoE (turn 6); 3. MoE Training Regimens for DiT: A Comparison of Decoupled and Joint Optimization (turn 7); 4. Evaluating MoE for Scalable and Efficient Text-to-Image Synthesis with DiT (turn 9).
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our framework, MoE-DiT, achieves state-of-the-art performance on text-to-image synthesis tasks while maintaining computational efficiency. We anticipate that MoE-DiT will become a widely-used benchmark for evaluating MoE-based DiT models.

TITLE: Investigating Token-Expert Correspondence in Diffusion Transformers

PROPOSAL: Conduct a thorough analysis on the tokenization strategy in DiTs and its impact on routing and expert specialization. This can be done by finetuning DiT-MoE on a dataset of images with masks, allowing the model to generate tokens that have clear spatial correspondence, and analyzing the gained routing patterns.

CONTROLS: Compare against token-choice routing in EC-DiT.
COST: 100 GPU-hours for finetuning.
PREDICTION: Improved routing patterns and a deeper understanding of token-expert correspondence, which might be the key to unlocking better MoE performance in DiTs. It could fail if the gains in routing patterns are not transferred to reachable generation quality improvements or if these results aren't generalizable across image types and datasets.

TITLE: Relating Visual Token Features to Expert Specialization

PROPOSAL: Investigate whether certain visual features extracted from tokens in DiTs (e.g., objectness, texture, color distribution) correlate with expert specialization. This can be achieved through a combination of dimensionality reduction techniques (e.g., PCA, t-SNE) and clustering methods (e.g., k-means, DBSCAN) to identify visually meaningful subspaces in the token space, and checking whether the outputs of different experts are more concentrated in these subspaces than in a uniform distribution.

CONTROLS: Compare the clustering performance when using dense DiT vs. MoE-DiT.
COST: 50 GPU-hours for data extraction and clustering.
PREDICTION: Identification of key visual features that facilitate expert specialization, which could justify modifications in token choices and router properties, ultimately enhancing the efficiency of MoE within DiTs. The results might not be scalable or generalizable to other tasks and data distributions.

TITLE: Investigating Token-Expert Correspondence in Diffusion Transformers with Spatial Tokenization

PROPOSAL: Refine the original proposal (1) by incorporating spatial tokenization, which divides the image into a regular grid of smaller patches, and routing experts based on these spatial positions. Compare the results against the original study, exploring how token location and spatial partitioning influence routing patterns and expert specialization.

TITLE: MoE Routing with Multi-Resolution Expert Selection

PROPOSAL: Investigate if selecting experts at multiple resolutions (e.g., low-resolution for context and high-resolution for detailed features) improves MoE's ability to capture global and local patterns in the image generation process. Design an experiment where the input tokens are grouped into multiple resolutions, each allocated to a specific group of experts.

CONTROLS: Compare against a single-resolution routing strategy and ablate which resolution levels contribute the most to the performance improvement.
COST: 80 GPU-hours for training and evaluating multi-resolution MoE.
PREDICTION: Improved performance of MoE by leveraging strengths in global and local pattern capturing. This might be due to the additional avenue for specialization and learning of smarter routes at different resolution scales, helping the model better split the representation and focus on specific visual aspects.

TITLE: MoE Routing with Multi-Resolution Expert Selection for Spatially Consistent Token Patterns

PROPOSAL: Refine the multi-resolution expert selection approach by coupling it with the spatial tokenization used in proposal 1. This modification aims to bring the advantages of multi-resolution routing to specific spatial locations, producing a model that expertly captures global and local patterns while maintaining spatial consistency.

CONTROLS: Compare the multi-resolution, spatially consistent routing approach against a single-resolution, spatially inconsistent one.
COST: 40 GPU-hours for incorporating spatial tokenization into multi-resolution routing.
PREDICTION: Enhanced performance of MoE through the combination of multi-resolution routing and spatial tokenization, which could lead to superior handling of global and local image patterns with coherent, spatially-aware routing decisions. These results, however, might be influenced by the quality and resolution of the spatial partitioning of the input image and potential artifacts introduced by inconsistent spatial and resolution features.

TITLE: Expert Selection Based on Visual Token Stability under Denoising Diffusion

PROPOSAL: Investigate whether visual tokens that maintain their structural consistency under consecutive denoising steps can be a better indicator of expert specialization and thus inform the routing decision. This can be done by analyzing the visual token stability over each step of the diffusion process and selecting experts based on their performance in handling stable tokens.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance against token-choice routing without stability constraint.
COST: 60 GPU-hours for analyzing token stability and integrating it into expert selection.
PREDICTION: Identification of experts that thrive on image patterns that persist under spatially-invariant processes, allowing MoE to better specialize in tasks that focus on visually coherent features and providing new information on the role of stability in diffusion transformers and connection to task success, potentially resulting in substantial performance gains for MoE based DiTs. The results may vary based on the extent that such stability corresponds to meaningful priors and the receptiveness of MoE to learn and integrate such cues effectively.

TITLE: Adversarial Training for Expert Routing in MoE Diffusion Transformers

PROPOSAL: Introduce an adversarial training framework to the MoE-DiT model, aiming to improve the robustness and efficacy of the expert routing mechanism by making it less susceptible to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting. This can be achieved by creating two neural networks: a generator (MoE-DiT) and a discriminator, and using a variant of the WGAN-GP loss to enhance the routing decisions.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance against a MoE-DiT model without adversarial training and analyze the impact on routing patterns and image quality.
COST: 120 GPU-hours for integrating adversarial training into the MoE-DiT.
PREDICTION: Improved stability and robustness of the expert routing mechanism, leading to enhanced overall performance and generalization capabilities of MoE-DiT models, particularly in the presence of new, unseen data. Challenges might arise if the adversarial training inadvertently degrades the model's ability to capture meaningful patterns and relationships between tokens and experts, thus diminish the overall quality of expert specialization and its benefits.

PROPOSAL: Refine the spatial tokenization approach used in proposal 1 by exploring more efficient methods for handling token positioning and expert allocation, such as incorporating attention mechanisms, graph neural networks, or hierarchical modeling. This modification aims to leverage recent advances in spatial reasoning and data-efficient modeling to reduce the overhead of spatial tokenization.

CONTROLS: Compare against the original spatial tokenization approach and the new, data-efficient modifications.
COST: 40 GPU-hours for incorporating data-efficient spatial tokenization.
PREDICTION: Development of more efficient and scalable methods for integrating spatial tokenization with the MoE architecture, potentially paving the way for larger and more complex models that still maintain the benefits of expert specialization. However, the improved spatial tokenization strategy may require careful tuning and could have unforeseen consequences on the router's choice of experts, which may in turn affect the model's performance in downstream applications.

PROPOSAL: Design a comprehensive large-scale evaluation framework to compare the efficacy of MoE-DiT against traditional dense DiT models on a variety of text-to-image generation tasks and datasets, such as iFORWARD 2.0, Stable Diffusion Text2Im, or other large-scale benchmarks.
